# sec-filing-ingestion roadmap

## Outcomes

Source: your partner's words, 2026-11-12. Background: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec.md, specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-adr.md.
Choices made: Python 3.14 (`.python-version`). uv workspace with the four packages under `packages/`.

| # | Outcome | Track | Rank | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| O1 | The quarterly and daily index files, ingested into one filing-index table | A | 1 | Small: about 130 quarterly files since 1993 plus one daily file per business day, minutes of downloading at 3 requests/second (SEC full-index and daily-index directories). Measured by Stage 1 |
| O2 | The individual submissions that the index rows name, downloaded | A | 2 | Large: millions of files, weeks for the full history at 3 requests/second (index row count × request rate; not yet measured). Measured for one quarter by Stage 2 and for the full range by Stage 6 |
| O3 | 10-K and 8-K filings handled: picked out of the submissions, with their main documents extracted | A | 3 | Unknown until the submissions are on disk. Measured by Stage 3 |

Tracks: A — SEC filing ingestion (known progression).

## Stages

- [ ] Stage 1: Filing-index table
      Objective: Ingest real quarterly and daily index files into one filing-index table.
      Outcomes: O1
      Consumes: nothing (package scaffolds only)
      Produces: the filing-index table on local storage; specs/sec-filing-ingestion-stage-1-findings.md
      Exit: O1 — one table holds rows from every quarterly index file and the open quarter's daily index files, with a row count per quarter. The findings file records the measured cost of the real run: elapsed time, request count and rate, and bytes downloaded.
      Leaves out: manifests and traceability (Stage 4); point-in-time awareness (Stage 5); full validation suites (Stage 7); scheduling and deployment (Stage 8)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 2: Submissions for one quarter
      Objective: Download the submissions that one real quarter's index rows name.
      Outcomes: O2
      Consumes: Stage 1's filing-index table
      Produces: the submissions for one quarter on local storage, each one locatable from its index row
      Exit: O2 — every index row of the chosen quarter has its submission on disk or is listed as failed. The plan's Handoff records the elapsed time, request rate and bytes of the run.
      Leaves out: manifests and traceability (Stage 4); full-history submission download (Stage 6); full validation suites (Stage 7); scheduling and deployment (Stage 8)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 3: 10-K and 8-K handling
      Objective: Pick the 10-K and 8-K filings out of the downloaded submissions and extract their main documents.
      Outcomes: O3
      Consumes: Stage 2's submissions for one quarter
      Produces: the extracted main documents of that quarter's 10-K and 8-K filings, each linked to its submission
      Exit: O3 — every 10-K and 8-K in the quarter has an extracted main document or is listed with the reason it has none. The plan's Handoff records the elapsed time and bytes of the run.
      Leaves out: manifests and traceability (Stage 4); full-history submission download (Stage 6); full validation suites (Stage 7); scheduling and deployment (Stage 8)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 4: Manifests and traceability
      Objective: Make every stored file and table row traceable to its source and re-processable from stored bytes.
      Outcomes: O1, O2, O3 (manifests and traceability)
      Consumes: Stages 1–3 outputs
      Produces: a manifest of sources and stored snapshots with their hashes; provenance on index rows, submissions and extracted documents
      Exit: O1 — each index row names its source file and hash, and re-processing from stored bytes makes no SEC request and yields the same table. O2 — each stored submission is listed with its hash. O3 — each extracted document names the submission it came from.
      Leaves out: point-in-time awareness (Stage 5); full-history submission download (Stage 6); full validation suites (Stage 7); scheduling and deployment (Stage 8)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 5: Point-in-time awareness
      Objective: Re-read quarterly indexes and keep every change to the filing-index table without losing earlier states.
      Outcomes: O1 (point-in-time awareness)
      Consumes: Stage 4's manifest and provenance
      Produces: a filing-index table that records additions, changes and withdrawals and answers as of an earlier date
      Exit: O1 — re-ingesting a changed quarterly index records its added, changed and removed rows, and a read as of an earlier date returns the earlier table.
      Leaves out: full validation suites (Stage 7); scheduling and deployment (Stage 8)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 6: Full-history submission download
      Objective: Download the submissions, and handle the 10-K and 8-K filings, across the full range of the index.
      Outcomes: O2, O3 (full-history submission download)
      Consumes: Stage 1's filing-index table; Stage 3's 10-K and 8-K handling; Stage 4's manifest
      Produces: the submissions and extracted 10-K and 8-K documents for the full range
      Exit: O2 — every index row in the range has its submission on disk or is listed as failed or pending, and an interrupted run resumes without downloading again. O3 — the 10-K and 8-K handling has run over the full range. The plan's Handoff records the elapsed time, request rate and bytes of the run.
      Leaves out: full validation suites (Stage 7); scheduling and deployment (Stage 8)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 7: Full validation suites
      Objective: Cover every index format, submission and filing shape in the range with committed tests.
      Outcomes: O1, O2, O3 (full validation suites)
      Consumes: Stages 1–6 outputs
      Produces: a committed test suite that runs without SEC access
      Exit: O1 — fixtures cover every index format in the range, and malformed rows and HTML error pages fail closed. O2 — fixtures cover failed, missing and truncated submissions. O3 — fixtures cover each 10-K and 8-K layout that the extraction handles. The suite passes with no SEC request.
      Leaves out: scheduling and deployment (Stage 8)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 8: Scheduling and deployment
      Objective: Run daily index ingestion, and the submissions and 10-K and 8-K handling that follow it, on a schedule without a person present.
      Outcomes: O1, O2, O3 (scheduling and deployment)
      Consumes: Stages 1–7 outputs
      Produces: a deployed, scheduled pipeline with a report per run
      Exit: O1 — consecutive scheduled daily runs are observed, each with a report, and a missed run is caught up. O2 — the submissions named by new index rows are downloaded by the scheduled runs. O3 — new 10-K and 8-K filings are handled by the scheduled runs.
      Leaves out: nothing
      ROUTING: brainstorming
